value.title: End-of-turn pij command blocks
value.summary: A seat ends its reply with a `pij` block of fire-and-forget commands and the harness runs them at turn end, so the closing sends and outputs cost no extra model calls.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Each extra pij tool call after the real work makes a seat re-read its whole cached context. Instead, a seat writes its closing commands as a final fenced `pij` block; at turn end the harness hands the final text to the daemon, which validates every line, then runs them in order as the seat through the CLI's own paths, stopping at the first refusal. Success shows the human one line; failure gives the seat one follow-up turn naming what ran. Claude (Stop hook plus a MessageDisplay hook that hides the block), Copilot (event stream plus onAgentStop; block visible) and OMP (session_stop plus an assistant-text renderer that hides it). Two coders, two lanes, two review rounds (C34).

sections.name: goals
value: A seat ends its reply with a `pij` block of fire-and-forget commands and the harness runs them at turn end, so the closing sends and outputs cost no extra model calls.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Verbs beyond send, output and requests close.
Hiding the block on Copilot (no display hook).
Any automatic use beyond what the seat writes.

value.claim: Daemon parser and runner (lane A, salmon). One daemon endpoint takes a seat's final reply text and returns results. Only a fenced block with the language tag `pij` that ends the message runs (nothing after it but whitespace); a block quoted mid-reply, or followed by prose, runs nothing. One command per line, written like the CLI without the leading `pij`, shell-style quoting. Allowed verbs: send, output, requests close; anything else, and never shell. Every line is validated first (verb, quoting, arguments): if any line fails, nothing runs. Then the commands run in order, as the calling seat (caller derived as for any CLI call), through the same code paths and refusals as `pij send`, `pij output` and `pij requests close`, and stop at the first refusal. The result names each command as ran, refused or not run, so a retry never double-sends. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents the endpoint and its refusals.

OMP (lane A, salmon). The pij OMP extension hands the final text from `session_stop` (last_assistant_message) to the endpoint, only when the text ends with a `pij` fence. Success shows one short line to the human (for example "pij ✓ 2 sent") via a custom message drawn once idle; failure returns {decision: block, reason} with the error and what already ran, only when stop_hook_active is false (OMP doesn't cap blocks). registerAssistantTextRenderer hides the block on screen and shows one line instead; pij's managed OMP config turns on extensionRenderers.assistantText.

Claude (lane B, lemur). Extend the existing Stop hook path (~/.pij-rs/claude-stop-pij.sh, plan 157); no second Stop hook. It hands last_assistant_message to the endpoint when the text ends with a `pij` fence; success returns {systemMessage: one line}; failure returns {decision: block, reason} only when stop_hook_active is false. A MessageDisplay hook hides the block on screen and shows one line ("⚙ pij: N command(s) handed to pij"): a tiny fast script that touches no daemon, keeping per-message_id state across flushes (in fence or not, and the line count, carried across flushes).

Copilot (lane B, lemur). The pij Copilot extension keeps the last root assistant.message (no agentId) from its event stream, deduped by messageId and reset per run, and on onAgentStop hands it to the endpoint when it ends with a `pij` fence. Success shows one line via session.log; failure returns {decision: block, reason} only when stopHookActive is false. An aborted turn runs nothing. The block stays visible (Copilot has no display hook; accepted).

Skill (lane B, lemur). One short section in the pij skill: end a reply with a `pij` block for fire-and-forget sends, outputs and request closes; keep a tool call when you need the answer before continuing; only the final block runs; what a failure looks like.

Setup is first-class, like the rest (Jordan, 2026-11-10): no hand edits, no setup a human or seat has to do. (a) Claude's MessageDisplay hook goes through crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs exactly as SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and StopFailure do: a managed script in harness/scripts/ (include_str!), installed to ~/.pij-rs/, registered by the same pure settings decision, idempotent and removable; the Stop hook's new work extends claude-stop-pij.sh in place (lane B). (b) OMP's extensionRenderers.assistantText goes into the OMP config pij already manages (`just link`, `just omp-doctor`), never ~/.omp by hand (lane A). (c) The Copilot side ships in the linked .copilot extension (lane B). (d) `just doctor` (and `just omp-doctor`) reports each one missing or stale, with the fix command. A fresh `just install` leaves all three harnesses working with no other step.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Steady state: one daemon call per turn end that ends with a `pij` block; nothing on turns without one; nothing per tick; no loop, no timer, no poll. Copilot and OMP extensions launch nothing (in-process, existing connections). The Claude Stop hook already launches once per stop (plan 157); the block adds no launch there. The Claude MessageDisplay hook launches one tiny process per flush of every Claude reply: measure it (launches per reply and per minute for a busy Claude seat, with `just spawn-rate --seconds 20` before and after) and state it per seat in the PR; it must touch no daemon.

Docs and states. The pij skill section (AC5); docs/how/pij-rs-api.md for the endpoint. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Phase 1 prototypes (2026-11-10, log-only, throwaway seats). Copilot CLI 1.0.109-0 (lemur): onAgentStop once per natural end; text from the last root assistant.message (arrived 9-159 ms before the hook, 7/7; getEvents agreed; transcript file lags); abort fires no hook; session.log one line never reaches the model; decision block queues the reason, re-entry has stopHookActive true, runtime caps blocks; no display hook, block visible as indented code lines. Evidence ~/.copilot/session-state/a400e300-fa07-43e7-8444-52c45ecf15d5/files/eot-probe/. OMP 18.14.1 (salmon): native session_stop with last_assistant_message and stop_hook_active, once at terminal settle, never for tool-call messages, aborts, subagents, retries or compaction; one line via sendMessage plus renderer once idle (~15 context tokens, no turn); decision block gives one hidden turn, no cap; registerAssistantTextRenderer hides the block in process, full text per draw (setting extensionRenderers.assistantText default off; disables smooth streaming). Evidence fleet-226-omp/scratch/226-omp-eot/FINDINGS.md. Claude Code 2.1.321 (prime POC): Stop hook input has last_assistant_message; systemMessage shows one line; decision block gives one more turn; MessageDisplay hook replaces a streamed delta on screen only (stored message unchanged), block split across flushes needs per-message state. POC scripts in the prime's scratchpad poc-eot/ (stop-hook.py, display-hook.py, settings2.json).

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
